title: The Day of Departure
subtitle: After the dust settles, he makes the decision.

content.text: Give me a minute; I'll go deal with the intruder.
Walking into my home with blood-soaked boots! Tsk. Such insolence. Does he think sending people to die makes him special?
He'll pay for this in blood!

branch.text: That's nowhere near enough. He'll have to scrub every bloodstain off the floor.
I don't want to hear any excuses. This whole mess is his own fault.
I AM calm. He brought the blood here, so he'll pay by cleaning up every drop.
I won't even lend him a rag—he can use that fancy coat of his for all I care.
So he claims those "big shots" forced him to stain his hands, huh? How convenient.
And this plan to "restore everything to how it was"? Utterly foolish.
But the fact that he followed it to the letter makes him no different from the ones who devised it.
To realize their "grand vision," those so-called realists kept piling weight on one side of the scale ...
Sacrificing one innocent life after another just so someone could remember a name that wasn't hers anymore. Absurd.
I have one thing to say to those arrogant megalomaniacs wanting to play gods: anyone who has forgotten their own name is as good as dead—and forcing them to wear it again won't change a thing.
What happened has happened. Those bloody footprints can never truly be erased.

items.text: The Day of Departure
The streets of Bereggrad are packed. The people hug and laugh, and the soldiers drink and sing to their hard-won victory.
But deep below the church, in a room from another age, there is nothing but silence.
The white marble chair is smooth and cold. The touch of a fingertip sends a distant call across time and space.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is it really you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ah!
She sits, and a pain prickles through her skin, a pain that is not her own.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What have you been through?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where are you?
Shh. We should let her get some rest.
Vertin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Who are you?
We all walk our own paths, seeking our own answers.
But our paths will surely cross again.
Timekeeper?
She gets to her feet, tearing her from those memories and thrusting her back into the real world.
The footsteps that follow carry a note of caution.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This room had always been locked to me, but now ... Tch. It is blindingly white.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Igor.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I wouldn't sit in that chair. Not unless you know it to be necessary.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Urd sat here. I wanted to try it myself.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Find anything useful?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Some documents on the experiment. The person who told me about this room might be interested.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But if you mean to ask about Urd specifically, I haven't learned anything more than I did on my first visit.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You were there. What do you know about the experiments in this room? What did they want from her?
Her usually reasoned words come quickly, driven by her hunger for answers.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What did you do to her?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The things the Pax House did to Urd ... I'm sure you've pieced it together somehow.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: After the second "Storm," the Foundation led an effort to build an emergency response system.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But after Manus Vindictae reared their head and in the wake of the vanishing of two eras, we realized no system could stop the "Storm."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We needed Urd.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And you tracked her down, only to find she'd become someone else, an investigative journalist, a humanitarian doctor, anything but the identity you were hoping for.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You tried every method to force that version of her, a blind woman you had no need of, into becoming Urd again, the one from 1999.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We, or the Pax House, believed that ...

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No matter the nature of the "Storm," whether Manus Vindictae forged new psyches from the realm of souls or twisted the entire material world to warp memories on a universal scale ...

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The key to every question about the "Storm" was tied up in Urd, the original Urd. The Loop Laboratory and the vessel ensoulment experiments conducted here were dedicated to finding that key.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Was that your goal to find her and end all this?
The old admiral closes his eyes, either to recall or avoid.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Igor, do you also want to return to the era before the "Storm"?
No reply comes. Igor moves to a corner as if searching for something.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Just as I suspected, they didn't have time to evacuate with these materials.
From a pile of disks, he lifts a white book as thick as a dictionary.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Take it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's heavy.
Its surface is as cold and hard as marble.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The weight of 43 souls combined.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The souls of those whose identities were "displaced" after the "Storm." I abducted them from all around the world—a way to regain my footing among the ranks.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I placed my trust, my hope even, in the Foundation, believing that these experiments would one day bring back the people I loved.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you chose to walk away.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: 43. Each soul left behind a husk. I buried every one of them.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I've buried so many people since the "Storm." I've lost count. I stopped counting.
He takes the black cube from his coat and murmurs an incantation. It floats above his palm.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Arcana's body was annihilated, but Her presence endures.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Even with my modest lineage, I feel Her presence everywhere, at all times.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: She bestowed on me a "boon" that let my army cross the "Storm." It worked, as She promised.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But after leaving Antarctica, the barrier that "boon" created could shelter only one person. I did still use it as a beacon to find a new sanctuary, but it cost us dearly in time and effort.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Meanwhile, Krutov seized the opportunity to wreak havoc along the Don.
A bitter smile colors Igor's face, and he stops channeling arcane energy into the "boon."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This is Arcana's mockery of me—the mixed-blood arcanist who dared mimic Noah.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you managed to build your own ark, didn't you?
He gives a dry laugh that is neither a yes nor a no.
Then he sets the "boon" down on the white book.
When she reaches out to it, the ever-present threads pull taut, then fade into the air.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You are the true savior destined to lead us from the flood. Take it.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Back to our deal, Timekeeper. I brought you to this laboratory as promised and told you secrets the Foundation would rather keep hidden.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Along with this "boon," I believe I have done enough to earn your favor.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What is it that you want?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Only that you consider me a partner in the future, so that we may help each other when the need arises.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm still the Timekeeper of the St. Pavlov Foundation. You're betting your life and freedom on nothing more than my favor.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Not my first gamble. I have confidence. You and I share the same enemy in Arcana.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: There's another matter. Krutov has passed the mask trial. He is more dangerous than ever before.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We defeated him at Tamarovka, but there was no sign of his body.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So you're suggesting ...

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Manus Vindictae lacks leaders with modern military training. I suspect Krutov will become key to their future conflicts with the Foundation.
Having left the Timekeeper to her devices, Igor slips past the street celebrations and leaves Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Father.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: As you said, Moldir, the Timekeeper is unlike most of her colleagues.
A soft laugh comes through the communicator. The events at the South Pole are still fresh in her mind.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: She is a truly extraordinary young woman. Based on my collaboration with her team in Antarctica, I'm sure she has prospects beyond the Foundation.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I hope your meeting brought something of value.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It did, to my surprise.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Recall all personnel on the field to the sanctuary. We need to accelerate recruitment and redeployment.
Moldir is temporarily rendered silent by the abruptness of this order.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Yes, Father.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Let the residents of any nearby villages join us if they wish. We need all the strength we can muster.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: All of them?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Civilian or soldier, human or arcanist—take them all in.
The admiral answers with unwavering conviction.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And keep an eye on Ptolemy until I return.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And should I not return, command of the Gryphon Legion will be transferred to you.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Father?
Igor, standing on the bank of the Don, gives the old city one last glance and ends the call.
What's the rush, old man?
A gun muzzle presses to the back of Igor's head.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I've been expecting you, Lieutenant Lilya.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So you recognize that Ptolemy is a good-for-nothing bastard, then? At least you're a better father than you are a soldier.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But being a half-decent father won't save you from the crimes you've committed or the lives you've taken.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I said it before, I'll say it again: I will personally escort you to the judgment seat.
